narrative:
Disneyland Paris Revenue in the 1+11 Forecast is EUR 3089.9M, +4.4% against the EUR 2960.0M budget.

Theme Parks is the largest business segment at EUR 1409.9M (46% of group). Merchandise is furthest ahead of plan (EUR 34.0M); Entertainment & Events is furthest behind (EUR -12.0M).

Key risk: the Entertainment & Events gap widens if the volume drivers on the Scenarios page move against plan.

signals.title: Park 2 opening lifted visits 35% and merch per cap 8% — cast overtime overshot by EUR 2.9M
signals.source: SDP Attendance & Labour — daily turnstiles × cast hours, Apr–Oct 2026
signals.excerpt: Disney Adventure World (Park 2) visits are 35.1% above the same months of 2025 since the new lands opened on 29 March, and merchandise per cap is up 8.2% to EUR 17.08. Cast overtime ran 10.0% of hours against a 5.5% standard on Park 2 peak days: EUR 2.9M above budget, concentrated in F&B and attractions.

signals.title: Heatwave week in July cut visits 10.8% below forecast and lifted beverage mix to 41% of F&B
signals.source: SDP Daily Attendance Forecast — ML forecast with weather exogenous variables
signals.excerpt: From 14 to 20 July 2026 daily visits ran 10.8% below forecast (about 56,500 a day) as temperatures passed 36°C. F&B covers fell less than visits and beverages rose from 33% to 41% of F&B sales, so F&B per cap rose about 8% while admissions fell for the week.

signals.title: UK & Ireland visits 8.8% below budget on GBP/EUR — offset by French domestic and Annual Pass growth
signals.source: SDP Guest Market Mix — booking source × country of residence × FX
signals.excerpt: UK & Ireland visits are 8.8% below budget since June as GBP/EUR moved from 0.84 to 0.88 and package prices rose for UK guests. French domestic visits are 4.9% above budget and Annual Pass visits about 9% up, recovering most of the admissions gap but with lower hotel attach.
